decision: Deep coordinates in plain scroll containers are owned by a new ledger entry P12 (paint, property trees, compositor, shaders: transforms become parent-relative exact offsets, folded to small window-relative f32 only at the GPU boundary), sequenced after L2. L2 owns the layout half as an interface constraint: child main-axis offsets are parent-relative and never rounded through absolute f32. ADR-0033 narrows its claim now: exact to 2^-20 px up to 2^43 px holds for scroll positions and virtual lists, plain-container content is placed and drawn exactly only below 2^22 device px until P12. SCROLL r15 only corrects the ADR text and adds one passing test pinning that bound, no rebasing in SCROLL. D001 was an accidental probe entry with no content and is void.
why: Codex r14 finding 2 reproduced: layout place.rs and compositor scroll.rs and compose.rs carry absolute window positions in f32 and the shader subtracts large f32s, so content past 2^23 px is not drawn and 1 px steps vanish at 36M px. The broken invariant is the ADR-0016 transform entry defined as an offset in window pixels, owned by the property trees, not by scroll motion. Fixing it inside SCROLL would rewrite layout place.rs concurrently with L2 and change ADR-0016, a standing decision that needs its own ADR. Virtual lists already rebase at the window origin (virtual_list.rs:954), so the millions-of-rows target is met today. Chrome caps near 33.5M px with LayoutUnit, an inherited limit we aim to beat, so plain containers are owned, not dropped.
